Continue the JANUS UAP registry by separating nuclear fireball optical phenomenology from POSS-I photographic transients, documenting transient candidates observed outside nuclear-test windows, auditing older UAP registry claims against current open sources, and replacing a generator-only nuclear hypothesis with a falsifiable baseline-plus-trigger/modulator model.

A 2026 preprint by Ariel Zhitnitsky proposes axion quark nuggets (AQNs) as a common explanation for POSS-I mysterious transients, nuclear-test timing, alignments and UAP/ball-lightning-like phenomena.
Most or all candidate transients arise from photographic emulsion, copy-plate processes, scanning, catalogue mismatch, plate-position systematics and observation-schedule confounding.
The relevant modifier may be broader magnetospheric/ionospheric state rather than nuclear testing itself; nuclear events would then be one possible perturbation among several.
Short sub-second optical flashes can appear sharper and rounder than stars in a long photographic exposure, so morphology alone may not uniquely identify emulsion defects.
Three approximately 16th-magnitude point sources within about 10 arcsec vanished within less than one hour and remained absent in deep follow-up observations over decades.
Nuclear tests do not generate all transients but may perturb atmospheric/ionospheric conditions and temporarily change the rate or visibility of a pre-existing class.
A subset of validated optical transients and a subset of independently validated UAP reports may arise from a common object population or common environmental driver.
Multiple bright transients are cited by Bruehl & Villarroel as a second July 1952 example in their discussion of UAP reports outside the nuclear-testing context.

Rate depends reproducibly on Kp/Ap, solar-wind, auroral or lightning/ionization variables in independent datasets.

A subset of validated optical transients and a subset of independently validated UAP reports may arise from a common object population or common environmental driver.

Association survives reporting-bias correction and quality weighting.

A 2026 preprint by Ariel Zhitnitsky proposes axion quark nuggets (AQNs) as a common explanation for POSS-I mysterious transients, nuclear-test timing, alignments and UAP/ball-lightning-like phenomena.

New single-author preprint; the model is not an independently established explanation of the POSS-I features. It is retained only because it proposes concrete tests and naturally motivates comparison of nuclear and non-nuclear ionization triggers.
Reports RR=1.45 for nuclear-window transient occurrence, p=0.008, plus UAP-count associations.
Nuclear correlation remains CONTESTED, not CONFIRMED.

Reports that the nuclear-test correlation becomes insignificant after normalization by relevant observation days and is almost completely determined by the Palomar observation schedule; also reports dataset-definition, catalogue-star, scan-artifact, plate-defect, edge/corner-density and spatial-structure concerns.
Prevents dismissal of the original effect solely because one critical reanalysis disagrees; exact exposure definitions must be harmonized and reproduced side-by-side.
Using the original dataset, reproduces RR=1.45 (p=0.011), reports negative-binomial effects after precipitation/lunar/cloud controls and a 10,000-iteration permutation p=0.006.
Kp/Ap and solar/geomagnetic conditions become mandatory covariates; the physical interpretation is not admitted from this preprint alone.
Reports strong suppression of transient detections at high Kp and argues geomagnetic state is an additional physical covariate while the nuclear coefficient survives in that model.

The published data themselves demonstrate a non-zero transient baseline outside nuclear-test windows. Therefore a nuclear test cannot be a necessary condition for this catalogued phenomenon. At most, the reported result proposes an excess/modulation around test windows, and that excess is presently contested by later reanalysis.
At least one UFOCAT report existed on 89.3% of dates, making a binary UAP/no-UAP exposure poorly discriminating.
Each additional independent UAP report was associated with an 8.5% increase in transient count in the fitted model.
Rejects any model in which nuclear tests are a necessary generator of the entire phenomenon.
A validated candidate population remains outside all nuclear windows after plate-quality and exposure controls.
Supports nuclear context as a rate modifier only.
A preregistered nuclear coefficient survives schedule/exposure, plate-quality, geomagnetic, weather and pseudo-date controls with stable direction and useful effect size.
Supports a broader trigger family and may demote the binary nuclear label from causal candidate to proxy variable.
Nuclear-window and non-nuclear validated events occupy a shared independently measured physical-state region (e.g. geomagnetic/ionization variables) that predicts events out of sample.
Rejects a physical nuclear/UAP interpretation for the affected dataset even if the original calendar correlation was statistically significant.
Effects disappear on original/independent scans or after plate/schedule controls.
Freeze exact transient catalogue version and every plate/copy/scanner provenance field.
Freeze exact nuclear-test table and define test-day, +/-1 day and lag windows before fitting.
Use actual observation opportunity / plate exposure as offset; do not use calendar days as if every day had equal sky exposure.
Analyze original plate material or the closest available independent scans where possible; distinguish original negatives from copy plates.
Model plate-edge distance, local defects, emulsion/copy batch and scanner provenance.
Use pseudo-event nuclear dates preserving season and observation schedule.
Include Kp/Ap, solar activity, lunar illumination, weather/cloud/precipitation and lightning where available.
Replace binary nuclear exposure with yield, burst altitude/type, distance from Palomar and physically motivated lag variables in secondary models.
Quality-weight UAP data; separate radar/multisensor/military records from unvetted witness-only reports.
Run the nuclear model without UAP, the UAP model without nuclear, a joint model, and a no-physical-trigger artifact/schedule model.
Hold out entire plates and date blocks for out-of-sample validation rather than random row splitting.
Require effect-direction stability under preregistered candidate-quality thresholds.
Report null results and failed replications with the same provenance depth as positive results.

This does not prove all UAP are mundane; it demonstrates that resolution of many cases is prosaic and that an unresolved label cannot be used as a proxy for extraordinary performance.
